kurz: Gelatine dissolves in warm liquid and forms a network as it cools that holds the liquid in place. In the mouth it melts again.
bild_im_kopf: Like a fishing net that tightens in the cold and holds the water in its mesh.
was_passiert: [[gelatine|Gelatine]] is made of long protein chains. When warm they float freely; as they cool they link into a network. Because it melts again at body temperature, panna cotta melts on the tongue. Boiling weakens the gelatine, and [[enzym|enzymes]] in raw pineapple or kiwi cut the network apart.
warum_wichtig: Explains why gelatine must never boil, why desserts need time in the fridge and why pineapple jelly does not set.
faustregeln: Soak leaf gelatine in cold water, squeeze it out and dissolve it in warm (not boiling) liquid.
Heat raw pineapple, kiwi or papaya first, or use tinned.

skala.name: melts (that is why it melts in the mouth)
